newsitem.title: USA: Washington counties added to disaster aid list.
newsitem.headline: Washington counties added to disaster aid list.

text.p: Two Washington state counties were added on Thursday to the list of local governments eligible for Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) disaster assistance due to damage from recent storms.
Douglas and Franklin counties are now eligible for public assistance and hazard mitigation aid, FEMA said.
Clark County was added to the list of local governments eligible for federal disaster assistance for individuals, federal and state disaster recovery officials said.
Clark County had previously been declared eligible for public assistance and hazard mitigation aid.
Thirty-eight counties in Washington state are now eligible for some form of federal disaster assistance after damage from storms and flooding that began in late December.
In Douglas and Franklin counties, federal funding will be available for the removal of debris and the repair of storm-damaged public facilities, such as roads and bridges.
In Clark County, residents and business owners will be eligible for disaster housing assistance, low-interest loans and grants from FEMA.
